languages.title: English
languages.summary: Mills, bridges and inns, as in an English market town.

languages.title: Celtic
languages.summary: Welsh-flavoured: Aber and Pen places, Melin and Pont streets.

languages.title: Slavic
languages.summary: Czech-flavoured: -hrad and -ves places, Mlýn and Most streets.

languages.title: Romance
languages.summary: Italian-flavoured: Monte and Castel places, Mulino and Ponte streets.

languages.title: Germanic
languages.summary: German-flavoured: -burg and -dorf places, Mühle and Brücke streets.

languages.title: Norse
languages.summary: Norwegian-flavoured: -fjord and -vik places, Mølle and Bro streets.

languages.title: Greek
languages.summary: Greek-flavoured (Greece and the Aegean): Agios and Kastro places, Mylos and Gefyra streets.

languages.title: Finnic
languages.summary: Finnish- and Estonian-flavoured (the northern forests and lakes): Koivu and Kallio places, Mylly and Silta streets.

languages.title: Iberian
languages.summary: Spanish- and Portuguese-flavoured (Iberia): Villa and Puerto places, Molino and Puente streets.

languages.title: Arabic
languages.summary: Arabic-flavoured (the Levant, Arabia and North Africa): Bab and Qasr places, Souq and Jisr streets.

languages.title: Persian
languages.summary: Persian-flavoured (Iran and the old Silk Road): Shahr and Kuh places, Pol and Bazar streets.

languages.title: Turkic
languages.summary: Turkic-flavoured (Anatolia and the steppe, Turkish with Kazakh and Uzbek touches): Kara and Ak places, Kapı and Köprü streets.
